p01.why: k = square(4) is a constant expression, so k is 16 before early's initializer reads it.

p02.why: mark is dynamically initialized before main starts with Clang and GCC, so initialized is 1.

p03.why: main accepts either value, so it returns 0 whether or not the initialization is deferred.

p04.why: Point p(3, 4) calls a constexpr constructor with constants, so p is constant-initialized and early reads 34.

p05.why: The function-local static is initialized at the first call to 7, and the constinit variable is 64 before any code runs, in any unit order.

p06.why: derived is base + 1, which is 8 or 1 depending on the order, and main accepts both.

p07.why: v is dynamic because base is not const, so early gets 0 or 8, and v is 8 by main.

p08.why: The dynamic initializers in one unit run in definition order, giving 1, 2, 3.

p09.why: b may be initialized early or not, so a is 0 or 3, and main accepts both.

p10.why: Before their dynamic initializers run, the pointer is null, the bool is false, and the double is 0.0; afterwards they hold their values.

p11.why: Across units seen gets 0 or 7, and main accepts both.

p12.why: base is a const int with a constant initializer, so k is constant-initialized to 8 before early reads it.

p13.why: y reads a volatile, so it is dynamic and still zero when early's initializer runs.

p14.why: Binding a reference to a variable with static storage is a constant initializer, so ref is set before early reads it.

p15.why: Clang and GCC run the other unit's initializer before main, even though main never names that unit.

p16.why: Registry::id takes its place at its definition, between a and c.

p17.why: first is constant-initialized to 4, and second, an inline variable after it, reads 4 and gets 5.

p18.why: later has a constant initializer, so early reads 5.

p19.why: Clang and GCC initialize tl at first use, giving 12, and main also accepts 21.

p20.why: mode() alone is constant-evaluated and takes the consteval branch, 1; with offset it runs at run time and takes the other branch, 2.
